title: The first page
label: ONE PAGE. THEN NOTHING.
lead: Hook 1, because almost everyone has a notebook like this and recognises it on sight.

hooks.label: ONE PAGE. THEN NOTHING.
hooks.say: You buy a new notebook, write one perfect page, and never open it again.

hooks.label: TOO NICE TO WRITE IN?
hooks.say: Why does a brand new notebook feel too good to write in?

hooks.label: PERFECT PAGE | FULL NOTEBOOK
hooks.say: A perfect first page, or a full messy notebook. You only get one.

beats.say: You buy a new *notebook*, write one perfect page, and never open it again.
beats.scene: A fresh notebook drops onto a warm wooden desk and falls open on one neat, inked first page. A pen rolls to a stop beside it.

beats.say: Because the next page might look *worse* than the first one did.
beats.scene: Close and low over the page edge. The pages fan past, every one of them blank and white.

beats.say: So it sits on the shelf, still looking new, waiting for the right day.
beats.scene: A dim shelf at dusk. The notebook stands between old books, dust floating in a thin beam of light.

beats.say: But a notebook was made to get *messy*, crossed out, coffee stained.
beats.scene: Top down on the open spread. Lines of scribble race across, words get crossed out, and a mug ring lands on the corner.

beats.say: Page two is allowed to be ugly. That's where it actually *starts*.
beats.scene: A page turns. A pen draws one wobbly line across the clean second page and the lamp warms up.

beats.say: Send this to the friend with a drawer full of *first pages*.
beats.scene: A desk drawer slides open, full of notebooks stacked on their sides, each with one page used, lit warm from above.
